Good question, and it exposes a misconception I should clear up before you commit.

## How A actually works (and why it's NOT raster OCR)

`generate_figma_design` does **not** infer elements from a raster. It runs a headless browser against the live web app, reads the actual rendered **DOM + computed styles**, and produces native Figma nodes — real TEXT layers, real FRAME/RECTANGLE vector layers, real auto-layout — by translating the DOM into Figma's node tree. Each `<div>` becomes a frame, each text node a TEXT layer, CSS colors/spacing map to paint/layout properties. It's a structural translation, not pixel-guessing.

So in Figma terms, Path A's output **is** natively editable — you can select the text, recolor a rectangle, move a frame. What it is **not** is *semantically structured*: a Figma "card" isn't a reusable Component, colors aren't bound to Variables, the 5 nav buttons are 5 independent instances rather than 1 component × 5. It's a flattened interpretation of one render.

## What "editable" really means across the three

| | A. Capture | B. Rebuild |
|---|---|---|
| Text editable | ✅ | ✅ |
| Colors/layout editable | ✅ | ✅ |
| Bound to design tokens | ❌ hardcoded hex | ❌ hardcoded hex (no DS exists) |
| Reusable components (Button, Card, NavItem) | ❌ flat | ✅ if I componentize |
| Faithful to real layout | ✅ pixel-exact | ⚠️ my reconstruction |

**The effort in B is on *this* end (me), not Figma.** And it's high because:
- 9 screens × hand-authoring each layout from React+CSS reading,
- the SVG `SubwayMap` and `ScriptureAtlas` are vector-dense — I'd be reconstructing SVG paths the skill says *never* to hand-draw,
- with **no design system in the file**, B's "tokens/components" benefit is hollow — there's nothing to bind to, so I'd hardcode hex anyway, same as A, just slower and less faithful.

The only real win B gives over A is **component reuse** (edit one NavItem, all update). That matters *if* you plan to iterate the design in Figma going forward. If you don't, it's pure cost.
